method: Complete pinned documentation reads with Git blob and SHA256 verification. Referenced charts and external sources not credited as viewed.
findings: Benchmark page explicitly warns it is out of date: v2.2 around2015, Linux3.14,8GB RAM and specific SSD/btrfs versus HDD/ext4 datasets. Comparisons cannot establish current ranking or our performance.

Page acknowledges every tool investigated different data and produced different counts. Its no-false-positive claim does not establish partition completeness; earlier original verifier controls accepted empty or split reports.
Replay avoids most IO and changes the operation being measured; warm scans, cold scans and replay need separate measurements. Logarithmic plots and historical CPU/RAM prose are not new measurements.

Developer optimization inventory suggests same-size partitioning, incremental early rejection, per-disk reader scheduling, separate hashing work and recycled IO buffers. These are design references only; source/runtime and paired performance qualification remain necessary.
Paranoid mode is described as retaining blocks rather than digest-then-confirm; claimed linear work and configurable memory do not establish a total strict-memory bound under all workloads.
Developer guide distinguishes DEBUG assertions from SYMBOLS, lists sanitizer and optional-feature controls. Documentation of these knobs is not evidence that corresponding runtime gates passed.

Guide philosophy says scanner itself should only emit outputs; this statement must be bounded by actual command modes and formatter code. No install, format, mutation or contributed-shell commands executed.
limits: No chart pixels viewed, upstream suite executed or new speed measurement.
